title: Secure SDLC & Audit Evidence Playbook for RBAC, Logging, and Data Residency
author: Ethan Zhang
content:
Summary:

This playbook defines the evidence collection, retention, and procedural controls required to demonstrate compliance for RBAC, authentication, audit logging, data residency and retention, secure SDLC checkpoints, and incident-response evidence collection. It is intended for the security, infra, SRE, legal, and engineering teams who are asked to produce artifacts for audits (SOC2/ISO/GDPR reviews) or internal compliance requests.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood-hosted control plane services, customer-facing APIs, private deployment tooling, and CI/CD systems that affect production workloads.
- Excludes third-party SaaS products where Redwood does not control log export (those are handled via vendor evidence requests and vendor attestations).

Key objectives:
1) Provide a repeatable, auditable workflow to produce common evidence types within defined SLAs.
2) Standardize artifact formats, storage locations, and retention for audit readiness.
3) Map Secure SDLC checkpoints to tangible artifacts (PRs, pipeline runs, vulnerability scans) auditors can validate.
4) Define incident-response evidence preservation steps to maintain chain-of-custody.

1) Ownership and escalation
- Evidence Owner (primary): Security (security@redwood.com).
- Operational Owners: eng-sre (alerts/runbooks), eng-platform (CI artifacts), eng-infra (IAM configs), eng-serving-runtime (model-serving logs).
- Auditor liaison: Head of Compliance (Marie Thompson).
- SLA for routine evidence requests: 5 business days for standard bundles, 10 business days for historical exports (>90d), 30 business days for privileged access reviews involving manual checks.

2) RBAC & Authentication — required artifacts and proof points
Purpose: demonstrate that access is principle-of-least-privilege, centrally provisioned, and regularly reviewed.

Required artifacts per auditor request:
- Current RBAC matrix (CSV): role -> permissions -> resource scope. (Location: s3://redwood-configs/rbac/current-rbac-matrix.csv)
- IDP provisioning snapshots: SCIM sync logs and group mappings from Okta. (Location: s3://redwood-idp-exports/okta-sync/YYYY-MM-DD.json)
- SSO/MFA policy screenshots or JSON policy export. (Okta policy export / GSuite export).
- Service-account inventory: list of non-human accounts, last-used timestamp, owner contact.
- Recent privileged access review report (date stamped).
- Audit trail of role changes (who, when, old_role, new_role) for the requested period (CSV).

Minimum retention for RBAC-related artifacts:
- Live RBAC matrix: current + 90 days (active snapshot history).
- Role change logs / authorization decisions: 13 months (default), 7 years if subject to legal hold.
- SCIM provisioning events: 24 months.

RBAC controls and tech specifics:
- IDP: Okta (SAML + OIDC). SCIM for group provisioning.
- Seats for automated provisioning: SCIM user/gro up sync every 6 hours; delta exports stored to S3 with KMS envelope encryption (KMS alias: alias/redwood-idp-kms).
- Minimum auth controls: SSO enforced for all human accounts, mandatory MFA (TOTP or WebAuthn).
- Privileged sessions use short-lived credentials via AWS STS and are logged with session metadata.

3) Audit Logging — pipeline and evidence model
Architecture summary:
- Application & control plane logs -> Datadog (primary ingestion) -> forwarding -> archived to S3 (audit-logs-prod) and to Splunk for on-demand search.
- Auth and IAM events -> exported from IDP and cloud provider to the same audit bucket with KMS encryption.
- Long-term archive: S3 Glacier Deep Archive when retention threshold is reached and after legal hold checks.

Required artifacts for a standard audit bundle:
- Log export: time-bounded bundle of logs (JSON/NDJSON) for requested services and time window. File naming convention: audit_{service}_{YYYYMMDD}_{incident-or-request-id}.ndjson
- Export manifest (manifest.txt) listing included files, checksums (sha256), KMS key id, and export operator.
- Datadog/Splunk query snapshots used to produce the export (saved query ID + query string).
- Proof of integrity: checksums and S3 object version ids.
- Retention policy document excerpt and lifecycle configuration for audit buckets.

Retention defaults (company policy):
- Control-plane audit logs: 13 months (default).
- Authentication/authorization events: 24 months.
- CI/CD pipeline execution traces: 13 months.
- Artifact metadata and SBOMs: 36 months.
- Legal/eDiscovery holds override retention durations (escalate to legal@redwood.com).

Exporting logs — operational commands (examples):
- Export via CLI (Datadog -> S3 via lambda): curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood/datadog/exports -d '{"query": "@service:api AND @level:ERROR", "from":"2025-02-01T00:00:00Z", "to":"2025-02-07T00:00:00Z", "dest":"s3://redwood-audit-logs-prod/exports/"}'
- Direct S3 copy (for support artifacts): aws s3 cp s3://redwood-audit-logs-prod/exports/audit_api_20250207.ndjson ./ --profile redwood-audit
- Verify checksum: sha256sum audit_api_20250207.ndjson

4) Secure SDLC — checkpoints mapped to artifacts
Goal: tie each SDLC gate to an artifact an auditor can validate.

Gates and artifacts:
- Design / PR approval: PR URL, list of approvers, design doc link, JIRA ticket id.
- Automated checks (pre-merge): CI status badge, static analysis output (Snyk/Semgrep results), dependency policy report.
- Secrets & policy scans: gitleaks scan results, blocked commits report, PR remediation notes.
- Build artifact / provenance: signed container image (cosign signature), artifact digest, SBOM (CycloneDX).
- Vulnerability triage: ticket IDs for high/critical issues and CVE tracking.
- Release notes & deploy manifest: deployed image digest, target cluster, rollout timestamp, rollback link.

Artifact storage locations and naming conventions:
- CI artifacts: s3://redwood-ci-artifacts/{pipeline}/{YYYY-MM-DD}/{run-id}/
- SBOMs: s3://redwood-sbom/{repo}/{commit}.cyclonedx.json
- Image signatures: container-registry/cosign/{image}@sha256:{digest}.sig

5) Incident-response evidence preservation
Objectives: preserve all necessary evidence while maintaining chain-of-custody and minimizing service disruption.

Preservation checklist (first 4 hours):
1. Declare incident and assign incident-ID (format: IR-YYYYMMDD-XXX).
2. Run immediate exports: Auth logs (IDP), control-plane logs (last 48h), host forensic images (if applicable). Exports should be written to s3://redwood-incident-bundles/{incident-id}/with kms encryption.
3. Capture volatile metadata (process lists, netstat, open ports) using approved host forensic tooling.
4. Create a manifest file (manifest.json) listing every file captured, collector, timestamp, and sha256.
5. Notify legal and preserve communications (Slack exports, email threads) as required.

Chain-of-custody and handling:
- All evidence objects must be written to the incident S3 prefix in append-only mode where possible (versioning enabled).
- Modify operations must be recorded in an incident evidence log (evidence-operations.log) noting actor, operation, and justification.
- If artifacts are transferred to external auditors, use pre-signed URL with a 7-day TTL and log the transfer event.

6) Compliance evidence workflow (step-by-step)
1. Auditor request intake: security@redwood.com receives request and creates evidence ticket (Confluence + JIRA EPIC).
2. Scoping call (within 2 business days) to confirm required time windows, systems, and formats.
3. Evidence collection plan assigned to operational owners with deadlines aligned to SLA.
4. Collate artifacts into a compressed bundle, produce manifest and checksums, and place in temporary restricted S3 location for auditor download.
5. Deliver secured pre-signed URLs and evidence indices to the auditor.
6. Post-delivery: record delivery in the Audit Deliveries register and schedule follow-up for clarifications.

Time expectations and common exceptions:
- Onboarding auditors will generally request standard bundles — these are delivered within 5 business days.
- Historical exports (>90 days) require additional approvals and may take up to 10 business days.
- Requests requiring cross-region log exports or legal hold validation may extend to 15–30 business days.

7) Artifact manifest (reference table)
| artifact_type | required_fields | default_retention | owner_team | example_location |
|---------------|-----------------|-------------------|------------|------------------|
| RBAC matrix | roles, permissions, scope, last_review_date | 90 days snapshot + current | security | s3://redwood-configs/rbac/current-rbac-matrix.csv |
| Auth events | user, event_type, timestamp, src_ip | 24 months | eng-infra | s3://redwood-idp-exports/okta-sync/ |
| App audit logs | service, level, timestamp, message | 13 months | eng-sre | s3://redwood-audit-logs-prod/ |
| CI traces | pipeline, run-id, artifacts, statuses | 13 months | eng-platform | s3://redwood-ci-artifacts/ |
| SBOMs | repo, commit, sbom_json | 36 months | eng-platform | s3://redwood-sbom/ |

8) Risk & Exceptions handling
- Any deviation from the retention defaults or RBAC enforcement requires a documented Risk & Exception request filed in the risk register and approved by Security + Legal. Typical approvals include: temporary extended log retention for incident investigation or reduced retention per customer contractual constraints.
- Exception artifacts: exception request ID, rationale, compensating controls, approval signatures, and expiration date. Store under s3://redwood-risk-exceptions/{exception-id}/.

9) Templates and checklists (quick links)
- Evidence bundle checklist: must include manifest.txt, sha256 checksums, export queries, and contact person.
- Incident evidence manifest template: /confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/templates/incident-manifest-template.txt
- RBAC review checklist: /confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/rbac-review-checklist-annual

10) Frequently asked auditor questions (short answers)
Q: How are logs protected at rest?
A: All audit buckets are encrypted with AWS KMS (alias/redwood-audit-kms). Access is limited by IAM policies and bucket policies; cross-account reads require explicit role assumption and are logged.

Q: How do you prove immutability?
A: S3 versioning + object lock (when required) plus checksum records and stored export manifests provide immutability evidence.

Q: What happens if an auditor requests a privileged access review?
A: Security will run the privileged roles change-log export, cross-reference with SSO group mappings, and coordinate interviews with approving managers. Delivery timeline: up to 30 business days depending on scope.

Appendix A — Example incident export commands
- Datadog export invocation (internal tooling): curl -s -X POST https://internal-api.redwood/logs/export -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"query":"service:control-plane","from":"2025-02-20T00:00:00Z","to":"2025-02-21T00:00:00Z","dest":"s3://redwood-incident-bundles/IR-20250221-001/"}'
- S3 manifest verification: aws s3api list-objects-v2 --bucket redwood-incident-bundles --prefix IR-20250221-001/ --query 'Contents[].{Key: Key, ETag: ETag}' --profile redwood-audit
